targetText: Guerrilla warfare will not remain the same throughout this long and cruel war, but will rise to a higher level and develop into mobile warfare. Thus the strategic role of guerrilla warfare is twofold, to support regular warfare and to transform itself into regular warfare.
summary: Guerrilla warfare in a national liberation struggle plays a dual strategic role: supporting the regular army behind enemy lines and gradually growing into regular mobile forces capable of decisive offensives.
explanation: Mao elevates guerrilla warfare from a purely tactical harassment method to the strategic centerpiece of the second stage of protracted war, showing how dispersed peasant partisan units temper and expand into regular field armies.
context: By the final stage of the war in 1945, the Communist-led guerrilla units had grown into a regular field force of over one million troops supported by two million militia.
